title: The Oath of the Scarlet Petal
text:
The righteous say: there is an evil, and we are against it.
The grey say: there is no evil, only a ledger.
We of the Scarlet Petal say: there is a pain, and whoever owns it owns the world.

We do not lie about the wound. We do not hide the blade.
We take what the sword-sects pretend is not taken.
We say aloud what the scholar-sects teach in whispers.
When a price is paid, we name the buyer, and we name the seller.

This is our kindness. It is not the kindness you were taught.
It is, however, the only kindness that does not finally become a lie.

title: The Ledger of Red Names
text:
The Crimson Registry is not, as outsiders whisper, a list of the Pavilion's victims. That ledger is smaller, and kept elsewhere.

The Registry is the ledger of the Pavilion's *debts* — every favour owed to the sect, every contract paid in advance, every sword-sect elder whose younger disciple once came quietly to a red-robed apothecary with a problem that could not be carried home.

The circle beside a name means the debt has been called in. The cross means the holder of the debt is dead.

There are more circles than crosses, which is how the Pavilion has lasted four hundred years without ever once winning a war.
